Proposition
[parallel transport]

↗ def:dc-ch2-2-5 ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-6-exist ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-6-unique ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-6-transport

1. ch2:2.6Let $c\colon I\to M$ be differentiable, $t_0\in I$, and $V_0\in T_{c(t_0)}M$. There is a unique parallel vector field $V$ along $c$ with $V(t_0)=V_0$. Its values are the parallel transports of $V_0$ along $c$.
Proof

↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-6-exist ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-6-unique ↗ lem:dc-ch2-2-6-transport \sketch In one chart, writing $V=\sum _jv^jX_j$ reduces parallelism to

\[ 0=\frac{dv^k}{dt} +\sum _{i,j}\Gamma _{ij}^kv^j\frac{dx_i}{dt}, \qquad k=1,\dots ,n.\tag {2} \]

This linear system has a unique solution for each initial value. On a compact subinterval, cover the curve by finitely many coordinate neighborhoods and glue the local solutions using uniqueness. These solutions extend throughout $I$.

□
